purpose: retrospectively test whether the public second-harmonic channel improves practical electrode-allocation identification beyond linear EIS alone

models.allocation_summary: positive-electrode Rct divided by the sum of positive- and negative-electrode Rct

split.rule: after removing the inductive high-frequency region using the pinned toolbox, hold out every fifth retained frequency index starting at index zero

optimization.near_optimal_rule: training objective no greater than best times 1.10 plus 0.005

metrics.fit_error: complex NRMSE: root mean squared complex residual divided by root mean squared complex data magnitude
metrics.joint_training_objective: mean of linear EIS and second-harmonic train NRMSE

confirmation_rule.per_spectrum_eligible: both arms meet the minimum successful-start and near-optimal-start counts
confirmation_rule.error_gate: median joint held-out linear EIS NRMSE <= 0.10 and median joint held-out second-harmonic NRMSE <= 0.20
confirmation_rule.contraction_gate: joint near-optimal allocation range is at most 75 percent of the EIS-only range in at least 20 of 30 spectra
confirmation_rule.joint_rule: all 30 spectra are eligible and both the error and contraction gates pass

reporting_policy: retain all spectra, starts, optimizer failures, held-out errors, and allocation ranges
do not select states of charge, replicates, circuits, starts, or frequencies after observing results
report practical and structural identifiability separately
a failed contraction rule does not invalidate second-harmonic information; it falsifies this frozen operational closure criterion
a passed rule is conditional on the declared equivalent-circuit family and does not identify a unique physical degradation mechanism
interpretation_boundary: This experiment evaluates practical parameter contraction within a pinned two-electrode circuit family on a public battery dataset. It does not establish universal EIS non-identifiability, validate the circuit as the true cell mechanism, or directly establish solid-electrolyte transport causality.
sealed_test_interaction: This deep-case experiment does not access or alter the paper-level sealed claim benchmark.
